title: Helmar pomelo (Helmar suha): Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Helmar pomelo: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Helmar pomelo is a pomelo variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Helmar is a registered pomelo variety, also sold or known as Helmar suha or NSIC Pm 03. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2006 as NSIC 2006 Pm 03. Its record notes a yield of 50 fruits.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Helmar suha or NSIC Pm 03, this is the same pomelo. Its seller and farm sources add notes, listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [pomelo variety finder](/crop-varieties/pomelo), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [fertilizer for fruit trees](/blog/fertilizer-for-fruit-trees).
When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Helmar was about 8 years old and about 3 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 50 fruits. It bears every year, with fruit in Jan., Feb. and Nov. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit pomelo fields most often: [citrus greening](/diseases/citrus-greening), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug), [Oriental fruit fly](/pests/oriental-fruit-fly). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

A fruit of Helmar weighs about 938.3 grams, and its shape is pyriform. The flesh is white and soft. Its sweetness measured 11.38 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 57.66 percent of the fruit. Its fruiting season is Jan., Feb. and Nov, bearing annual.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** Pear shaped, about 940 g, pale yellow peel, juicy, sweet white flesh, about 11.4 Brix.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: Aklan State University's sweet white fleshed pomelo. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Helmar pomelo

Davao is the home of suha. Pick a registered selection by flesh color and sweetness, and plant marcotted trees. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Helmar suha the same as Helmar?
items.a: Yes. Helmar suha is another name for Helmar, registered as NSIC 2006 Pm 03. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows a recorded yield of 50 fruits. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Helmar?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
